name: Trainer Intelligence Hypothesis B - late price shortening into BSP
description: Tests whether a runner whose price shortens by 15%+ between the widest pre-off price (pre_max) and the final Betfair Starting Price (BSP) outperforms what pre_max's own de-vigged implied probability predicted -- brief Section 12B's market-behaviour hypothesis. IMPORTANT CAVEAT this hypothesis itself surfaces: BSP is the price at the actual off, essentially the market's own final, most-informed estimate -- so a positive result here is expected/mechanical (markets get more accurate closer to the event) rather than necessarily evidence of an EARLY, actionable signal. It does not by itself demonstrate exploitable pre-race timing information; morning_wap, which would have let this be tested against a genuinely early decision point, is 0% populated in this dataset (see the module's own data-coverage correction).
rule_definition: QUALIFYING: (pre_max - bsp) / pre_max >= 0.15 (price shortened 15%+ into the off). CONTROL: everyone else. Compared via actual_wins vs sum-of-pre_max-implied-probability expected_wins for each group.
source_finding: scripts/trainer_intelligence_b_report.py, full run over historical_betfair_price (2026-03-01 to 2026-04-29)

historical_evidence.conclusion: Directionally consistent with 'markets get more accurate closer to the off' -- qualifying group beat its early-price expectation, control group fell short of its own. Read as a mechanical confirmation of market efficiency near the off, NOT as an early, actionable trading signal, since BSP is essentially final. A genuinely early decision-time test (morning price vs pre-off) is not possible with this dataset -- morning_wap is 0% populated. Would need either a different historical source with real morning prices, or the live Smarkets collector accumulating enough real forward data.
historical_evidence.statistical_caveat: Pooled at runner level, NOT race-level resampled -- observations within the same race are not independent.

prospective_results.note: mechanical near-off-accuracy confirmation, not an early actionable signal per the hypothesis's own caveat; needs real early-snapshot data (live Smarkets accumulation or a different historical source) before this can be tested properly
